Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that somatostatin receptor subtype 2a immunohistochemistry (IHC) may not offer additional value compared to somatostatin receptor scintigraphy uptake in predicting gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEP-NET) response.

The completion of the prompt suggests that a study found that sst2a IHC of tumor samples had no additional value in predicting tumor response after peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT). This implies that while there may be some differences between IHC and scintigraphy techniques, they do not provide significantly different information for predicting GEP-NET response.

It's essential to note that the results of this study may vary depending on the specific patient population and tumor characteristics. Further research is needed to confirm these findings and to explore the potential benefits or drawbacks of using sst2a IHC in comparison to scintigraphy uptake for predicting GEP-NET response.
